blocks.lead: Carpet installation cost in Snohomish is set by four things: the fiber, the pad under it, how your rooms lay out against a 12 ft roll, and what has to come out first.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring does not price carpet off a rate card because those four variables move the number too much. We bring the samples to your house, measure every room, and give you a firm written price on the spot. This post explains what moves that price so you know what you are looking at.

tiles.label: Pad
tiles.value: 6 to 8 lb rebond is the sweet spot

blocks.html: People in Snohomish ask this question with a specific house in mind: a farmhouse off Fobes Hill with two dogs and a mud problem, a 1990s place in Clearview where the builder carpet finally gave out, or a Blackmans Lake rental between tenants. Each of those is a different job with a different price, and any contractor who gives you a single number before seeing the house is guessing. Here is what actually goes into the quote.

blocks.text: The four things that set the price

items.title: 1. Fiber and construction
items.text: Polyester is the budget fiber, nylon and triexta the durable ones, wool the premium. Within each fiber, face weight and twist level move the price again. A dense, high-twist nylon can cost more than double a light polyester of the same color.

items.title: 2. The pad
items.text: Pad is priced separately and usually makes up a meaningful slice of the bill. Thicker is not better. Density is what protects the carpet, and a good 8 lb rebond pad often adds years to a mid-grade carpet's life.

items.title: 3. Layout and waste
items.text: Carpet comes on 12 ft rolls. A 13 ft wide room needs a seam and a second cut, and a long hallway can waste 20 percent of a roll. Snohomish farmhouses with odd additions tend to waste more than a square 1990s rambler.

items.title: 4. Tear-out and prep
items.text: Pulling old carpet, pad and staples is routine. Old glued-down carpet, pet-soaked subfloor that needs sealing, or a squeaky floor over a crawlspace that needs screwing down all add labor, and all are quoted after we look.

blocks.note: Tiers are relative, not dollar figures. National averages for installed carpet span a wide range and are not Wills prices; we quote your exact rooms and product at the estimate.

blocks.text: Pad: where the hidden money is

items.html: Cheap pad kills good carpet. A 5 lb or 6 lb pad under a heavy nylon lets the backing flex, which is what breaks fibers loose. Most low quotes get low by dropping the pad grade.
Thickness is not quality. 7/16 in at 8 lb density outperforms 1/2 in at 6 lb. Ask for the density in pounds per cubic foot, not just the thickness.
Moisture barrier pad over crawlspaces. Many Snohomish homes sit over a vented crawlspace. A pad with a film barrier keeps ground moisture and pet accidents from soaking into the subfloor.
Pet-specific pad. Odor-blocking pads cost more but let you clean an accident out of the carpet instead of the plywood beneath it.
Firmer pad on stairs. Soft, thick pad on stairs lets the carpet flex and wear at the nosing. We spec a denser, thinner pad on treads.

blocks.text: How a carpet measure actually works

items.text: Every room, closet and hallway is measured to the inch, including the tuck under baseboards and doorways.
We lay the rooms out against a 12 ft roll to place seams under furniture or away from windows, where light would show them.
Simple rectangular rooms waste about 10 percent. Halls, stairs and odd angles push it to 15 to 20 percent. You pay for the roll, not the room.
Straight, pie-shaped and open-sided stairs are counted and priced separately because each is hand-fitted.
Carpet, pad, tear-out, disposal and stairs on separate lines. The number you sign is the number you pay.

blocks.text: Where Snohomish homes cost more, and where they cost less

a.title: Expect more when
items: Acreage homes with a mudroom, dogs and a wood stove: durable fiber plus moisture pad
Historic downtown houses with out-of-square rooms and multiple seams
Stairs, especially open-sided or pie-shaped runs
Old glued carpet or pet damage in the subfloor

b.title: Expect less when
items: Square 1990s bedrooms in Clearview or Fobes Hill that fit a 12 ft roll with no seams
Bedrooms only, with polyester or an entry-level triexta
Existing pad in good shape that can stay (we check its density first)
Rooms you empty yourself before we arrive

blocks.title: The Snohomish dog rule:
blocks.text: If your dogs come in from a wet field twice a day, put the money in the fiber and pad, not the pile height. A dense triexta or solution-dyed nylon on an 8 lb moisture-barrier pad will outlast a plush polyester twice over. We will show you both on the sample boards and tell you honestly which one your house needs.
How to get a firm number, not a range

items.html: Get measured in the house. Room sizes off a listing or a tape you ran yourself do not account for seams and waste. Our estimate is free and we come to you, about 25 minutes from the Lynnwood showroom.
Ask for carpet, pad and labor on separate lines. That is how you compare two quotes and spot the one that saved money on the pad.
Write down the fiber, face weight and pad density. "Mid-grade carpet" is not a spec. Our pet carpet guide explains what to look for.
Ask what they will do about the subfloor. Squeaks, staples, and pet-stained plywood should be handled before pad goes down, and the quote should say so.

Check the warranty. Wills Flooring is licensed and insured, has installed carpet since 2013 and backs every job with a 1-year workmanship warranty on top of the manufacturer's. See the carpet installation page for what is included.

faq.q: Why won't Wills Flooring publish a carpet price per square foot?
faq.a: Because fiber, pad, seam layout and tear-out change the price more for carpet than for any other floor we install. A single published number would be wrong for most houses. Instead we measure, bring samples, and give a firm written price at the free estimate, so the number you see is the number you pay.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to carpet a house in Snohomish?
faq.a: Choose a polyester or entry triexta in a light-hiding color, keep bedrooms simple so they fit a 12 ft roll without seams, empty the rooms yourself, and skip stairs if they are already in decent shape. Do not skip the pad grade; that saving costs you the carpet within a few years.

faq.q: Does the estimate include removing the old carpet?
faq.a: Yes, tear-out and disposal are itemized on the same written quote. Carpet, pad and staples come up quickly. If we find glued carpet, pet damage or a squeaky subfloor, we price that repair as a separate line rather than surprising you on install day.

faq.q: How much extra do stairs cost to carpet?
faq.a: Stairs are counted and priced per tread because each one is hand-cut and stretched. Open-sided and pie-shaped treads take longer than a straight boxed run. We show the stair line separately so you can compare it against carpeting the stairs later or switching them to hardwood.

faq.q: Should I pick a thicker pad for comfort?
faq.a: Not usually. Density protects carpet; thickness mostly adds bounce. A 7/16 in pad at 8 lb density is our standard recommendation for living areas, with a firmer, thinner pad on stairs. Thick, soft pad under a heavy carpet lets the backing flex and shortens its life.

faq.q: How long does carpet installation take in a typical Snohomish home?
faq.a: Three or four bedrooms and a hall are usually done in one day, including tear-out. Whole-house jobs with stairs and a family room take two days. You can walk on the carpet immediately and move furniture back the same evening.
